prompt: What are some obscure or lesser known features of Windows Notepad?
response: Windows Notepad, while simple and basic, does have some lesser-known features that can be quite useful for certain tasks. Here are a few: 1. **Hexadecimal View**: Notepad can display text in hexadecimal format. To view a file in hexadecimal, open the file in Notepad, then press `Ctrl + H`. This can be useful for viewing or editing binary data. 2. **Find and Replace with Wildcards**: Notepad supports wildcards in the "Find and Replace" dialog. For example, you can use `*` to match any sequence of characters and `?` to match a single character. This can be handy for more complex text searches and replacements. 3. **Multiple Files**: You can open multiple files at once by holding down `Ctrl` and clicking on the files in the File Explorer. This allows you to compare or edit multiple files simultaneously. 4. **Auto-Completion for HTML and XML**: If you start typing an HTML or XML tag, Notepad will automatically complete it with the closing tag. For example, typing `` will automatically become ``. 5. **Custom Font and Size**: While Notepad's font and size are usually fixed, you can change them by going to `File > Properties > Font` and selecting a different font and size. This can be useful for readability in certain situations. 6. **Word Wrap**: You can enable word wrap by going to `View > Word Wrap`. This can be helpful for reading long lines of text without horizontal scrolling. 7. **Line Numbers**: To display line numbers, go to `View > Line Numbers`. This can be useful for referencing specific lines in a document. 8. **Auto-Save**: While Notepad doesn't have a built-in auto-save feature, you can use a third-party tool or script to add this functionality. For example, you can use a simple script to save the file at regular intervals. 9. **Custom Menus**: You can customize the menu bar by adding or removing items. To do this, go to `Tools > Customize` and then select the `Commands` tab. 10. **Clipboard History**: Notepad has a clipboard history feature that allows you to access the last 24 items you've copied. You can view this by going to `Edit > Paste Special > Paste from Clipboard History`. These features, while not as extensive as those found in more advanced text editors, can still be quite useful for specific tasks.
